name: Ombu of San Nicola, Isole Tremiti
access: Island of San Nicola is open to visitors by ferry/hydrofoil (Termoli, Vieste, Peschici, Rodi Garganico, Manfredonia in season). Whether the exact tree stands on a public path or inside a paid or closed part of the abbey-fortress complex is NOT established; flagged.
transport: Ferry or hydrofoil to San Nicola in summer from Termoli, Vieste, Peschici and Rodi Garganico (about 45 to 90 minutes depending on port); services thin out outside May to September. Over 30 minutes, so an island day trip, not a walk from the coast.
verify_notes: SOURCES: Puglia register 01/E363/FG/16 records an 'insieme omogeneo di Phytolacca dioica' (a homogeneous group, not a single measured tree) on Isola San Nicola, no girth or height given. ALIVE and species: two independent iNaturalist observers recorded Phytolacca dioica on San Nicola in 2025 (obs 303541268, 2025-08-02, 42.120369,15.503167; obs 309180835, 2025-08-26, 42.120531,15.503119), each confirmed by a second identifier, marked casual (cultivated); both within about 30 m of the register point and about 18 m of each other. Photos CC BY-NC (not usable). Web searches found no article, plaque or guide naming this ombu; only the register and iNaturalist. Ombu is a non-native South American tree, so on a Tremiti page its interest is the oddity (swollen buttressed base, evergreen, resists sea wind); no age basis, left empty. Group, not single tree: the exact trunk to stand at is not established, so approximate; two GPS fixes of the species ~18 m apart suggests one small cluster. Access to the exact spot unverified.
